headline: G7 foreign ministers condemn Iran's attacks on neighbours and Hormuz obstruction'
dek: [VERIFIED FACT -- the condemnation] The G7 foreign ministers 'strongly condemned Iran's attacks against its neighbours and the disruption of international trade, energy security, and the global economy caused by the obstruction of transit passage through the Strait of Hormuz,' and called on Iran…
sources: Joint statement following the G7 Foreign Ministers' Meeting, Paris, Nov 9-10, 2026 (Global Affairs Canada / GOV.UK)
fault_line: G7 unity vs empty words -- seven governments condemn, but does anything change on the water while Hormuz sits at 4.5% of normal traffic?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the condemnation] The G7 foreign ministers 'strongly condemned Iran's attacks against its neighbours and the disruption of international trade, energy security, and the global economy caused by the obstruction of transit passage through the Strait of Hormuz,' and called on Iran to 'cease its persistent attacks against civilian vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.' They opposed any tolls, fees or other restrictions on maritime transit. [VERIFIED FACT -- Fairford] The ministers 'recognized the United Kingdom's attribution of Iran's involvement in the incident at RAF Fairford on 27 September' and expressed 'grave concern over Iranian involvement in violent plots against many of our citizens and territories.' [VERIFIED FACT -- Ansar Allah] The ministers termed the continued Ansar Allah strikes against Saudi Arabia 'unacceptable' and urged all actors, including Iran, to stop arming and supporting the group. [VERIFIED FACT -- nuclear] Iran 'must never be allowed to develop or acquire a nuclear weapon'; urged to resume full cooperation with the IAEA. [VERIFIED FACT -- CENTCOM] The statement underscored US CENTCOM's defensive work to clear mines and escort civilian ships in the strait, and support for the French-British maritime initiative.
sections.what_verified: 3 tiered families: G7 joint statement itself (T1 official, published by Global Affairs Canada and GOV.UK), Arab News (T3), Jerusalem Post (T3). This Is Beirut and United States Tribune carry it but have NO declared tier in the registry and do not count.
sections.what_disputed: The statement is a collective condemnation, not a new sanction or military decision: it commits only to 'continuing coordination to constrain' Iran absent a diplomatic solution, and backs diplomatic efforts / commends regional mediators. No new deadline or ultimatum. The Fairford attribution rests on the UK's attribution, not on evidence published in the statement; Iran denies any role in the Fairford plot (JPost). The US Justice Department said Nov 10 a member of an Iran-backed group plotted the Fairford attack while detained in the US -- that is a separate, ongoing case, not proof of the G7's attribution.
sections.why_matters: All seven just put it in writing: Iran's Hormuz obstruction is now a G7 verdict -- and they endorsed the UK's claim that Iran was behind the Fairford airbase plot.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (AJ liveblog 14:30 GMT = 18:30 ; statement published Nov 11; Canada.ca; gov.uk; Arab News 13:01Z) -- G7 foreign ministers condemn Iran's attacks on neighbours and Hormuz obstruction; recognise UK attribution of Iran's role in the RAF Fairford incident (Sep 27); condemn Ansar Allah strikes on Saudi Arabia

totw_analysis: Our read: All seven just put it in writing: Iran's Hormuz obstruction is now a G7 verdict -- and they endorsed the UK's claim that Iran was behind the Fairford airbase plot. The fault line our audience is arguing over: G7 unity vs empty words -- seven governments condemn, but does anything change on the water while Hormuz sits at 4.5% of normal traffic?
